title.narrative: Driving sustainable lifestyle choices; HabitSwapp Market validation in India

description.narrative: The Indian society is prone to diabetes and heart disease due to their historic diets and lifestyles, and an increase in overall income and easy access to products has led developing societies like India to emulate Western lifestyle consumption patterns. The general knowledge on some of the urgent environmental issues of today is very low most people are not aware that many of the sustainability issues that can affect them and their health are mostly caused by consumption of food, energy, water, etc. Lack of awareness how consumption affects health and the environment and limited ways to track or measure these, make it difficult to tackle these challenges effectively. HabitSwapp, formerly known as GreenerU, is an app designed to engage consumers and help them live healthier and more sustainable by using gamification and personalized advice to enable behavioural change of consumption habits in a fun competitive way. Better consumer choices will be enabled through the app by showing the carbon food print and nutritional value of items bought by the consumer and promoting and rewarding alternative choices. The app is offered through retailers who drive the majority of the consumption, as well as through health related partnerships.Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provides support to validate the app in the Indian market and adapt it to the local context. The project includes support for the market validation through a retailer pilot, identifying the right product-market fit by collecting data from test-users, selecting partners and developing a bankable business plan to prepare for scale-up investments after the pilot. The project directly supports 9 full-time jobs, indirectly supports 36 jobs, and enables knowledge transfer by providing workshops to 34 people about promoting sustainable food choices. Furthermore, during the pilot, the project will already have a positive impact on 10,000 Indian test users’ lifestyle choices and awareness of sustainable consumption. Upon successful completion, further investments will be explored and may lead to 200 new jobs within 5 years and has the potential to educate at least 10 million people on sustainable food choices.
